channel.title: The Pritiraj Review
channel.description: Evidence-led essays by Pritiraj Brahma on Indian governance, state capacity, institutional design and fiscal federalism.

item.title: Two Surveys, One Country
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: India’s two official sources on child undernutrition disagree about wasting by fourteen percentage points. One of them is now used to report progress, and it is not the one designed to measure it.

item.title: Eight Hundred and Fifty Seats — What Delimitation Actually Decides
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: The Delimitation Bill, 2026 proposes a 850-member Lok Sabha with 272 seats reserved for women. The seat count is the least consequential thing about it.

item.title: The Arithmetic of Absence — Why Air India Is Losing a Market It Was Built to Lead
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: Air India's FY26 loss hit ₹22,238 crore as domestic share fell to 23.9%. A structured analysis of why the turnaround is stalling — and the correction required.

item.title: The Arithmetic That Should Alarm Us — India's Learning Crisis as a Solvency Problem
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: India enrols nearly every child and half leave unable to do grade-level mathematics. Why the learning crisis is now a fiscal question — and the five structural corrections it requires.

item.title: The Quiet Part of a Loud Victory — Symbol, Substance and the Exam Reform
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: The street took a scalp; the State had already rebuilt the system. Why the resignation of the Union Education Minister matters less than the five corrections that preceded it.

item.title: The Dashboard Problem — When Measurement Replaces Delivery
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: India has more real-time government dashboards than any comparable state. Pendency, learning outcomes and delivery gaps have not moved with them. Visibility is not accountability.

item.title: The District Is Where the State Lives — The Tier India Refuses to Staff
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: India debates the Centre and the states endlessly and ignores the tier where governance actually succeeds or fails. The district runs at 19% IAS vacancy against a mandate that expands every year.

item.title: The CJP Protest — Ten Million Followers, One Unwinnable Demand
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: Ten million followers in five days, and no institutional outcome. A strategist's diagnosis of five design errors — and the pivot that could still convert pressure into text.

item.title: The Forty-One Percent Illusion — State Finances After the Sixteenth Commission
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: The 16th Finance Commission held devolution at 41% and discontinued revenue deficit grants. Why a headline of continuity conceals the tightest state fiscal settlement in a decade.

item.title: The Certificate Is Not the Job — Why India Skills Millions and Employs Few
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: PMKVY trained 13.7 million people in seven years and placed 18 per cent of them. The failure is not effort; it is a system built to count certificates instead of livelihoods.

item.title: The Campus Economy — India's Quietest Special Economic Zones
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: Roughly 37% of notified SEZ land is in use. Meanwhile four university gates have built the concentrated capital, talent and IP pools that SEZ policy spent twenty years trying to engineer.

item.title: India's Demographic Clock — The Deadline Beneath Every Other Debate
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: A median age of 28 in an ageing world is India's greatest advantage and its deadline. The working-age share peaks in the 2040s; everything else is a question of what gets delivered before then.

item.title: Four Codes, Thirty-Six Rulebooks — The Labour Reform That Is Not Yet a Reform
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: Twenty-nine central labour laws were repealed on 21 November 2025. The central rules arrived on 8 May 2026. The states are where the reform is now decided.

item.title: The Northeast Is Not the Periphery — A Gateway That Is Not Yet Open
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: Over ₹6 lakh crore committed in a decade, and the region's exports fell from $50.8m to $47.6m. The gateway framing is right; the execution gap is the whole problem.

item.title: The Last Mile Is the Whole Journey — What Seventy-One Farms Taught Me
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: Meghalaya imports 18,000 tonnes of pork a year while almost every household keeps pigs. The gap between those two facts is where Indian governance is actually decided.

item.title: The Tariff That Was Never Lawful — What India Conceded, and What It Should Learn
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: India negotiated relief from a 50% US tariff in February 2026. Three weeks later the US Supreme Court held the instrument behind it was never authorised. A lesson in negotiating against legal durability.

item.title: The Specialist Who Was Never Sanctioned
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: The specialist shortfall at India’s rural community health centres appeared to shrink by a third this year. The number of specialists barely moved. The requirement was rewritten.

item.title: Cities Without Money — The Third Tier and the Capacity It Lacks
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: India's cities produce roughly 60% of GDP and raise 0.6% of it. The Sixteenth Commission has now sent them ₹3.6 lakh crore against conditions most cannot yet meet.

item.title: The Thirty-Nine Percent Question — Health Spending and What It Buys
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: Out-of-pocket health spending has fallen from 62.6% to around 39%. Public health spending sits at 1.8% of GDP against a 2.5% target. Both numbers describe the same unfinished settlement.

item.title: Who Regulates the Regulators
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: India built independent regulators for its most important sectors and then left their appointments, budgets and accountability inside the ministries they were meant to check.

item.title: Airsheds Do Not Respect District Lines
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: India measures air pollution by city and manages it by municipality. The pollution arrives from a region several hundred kilometres wide. The mismatch is the whole problem.

item.title: Three in Four
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: India’s prison population fell in 2023 and overcrowding eased by ten points. Nearly three-quarters of those inside have still not been convicted of anything.

item.title: The Missing Middle of Indian Enterprise
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: Only 14% of India's MSMEs have formal credit, against a gap estimated between ₹25 and ₹30 lakh crore. Indian firms stay small because staying small is the rational response to the system around them.

item.title: The Discom Turnaround — and What It Does Not Yet Prove
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: India's power distributors posted a collective profit of ₹2,701 crore in FY25 against accumulated losses of ₹6.47 lakh crore. A real turnaround, and a small one.

item.title: The Aquifer Is the Real Budget Constraint
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: India extracts 247.22 BCM of groundwater a year — a quarter of the world's total. 730 assessment units are over-exploited. The binding constraint on Indian agriculture is not credit or price.

item.title: Five Crore Cases and the Arithmetic of Delay
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: India's courts carry more than 5 crore pending cases with roughly 14 judges per million people against a recommended 50. The backlog is not a moral failing; it is a capacity equation.

item.title: Citizens Who Move, Entitlements That Do Not
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: India built a portable ration card and stopped there. A migrant worker still cannot vote, see a doctor, enrol a child or claim a pension where they actually live.

item.title: Sixty-Eight Paise in the Rupee
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: North-eastern and Himalayan states raise roughly a third of what they spend. The problem is not the dependence — it is that most of the money arrives with someone else’s conditions attached.

item.title: The Half That Does Not Show Up — India's Female Participation Problem
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: Female labour force participation has risen to 40%. Urban female participation sits near 25%, and 44.4% of women outside the workforce name care work as the reason. The constraint is not ambition.

item.title: The Title Is the Asset — Why Indian Land Cannot Be Used as Capital
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: India's land records are presumptive, not conclusive. A landholding you cannot prove you own is a landholding you cannot borrow against, sell cleanly, or defend in court.

item.title: Twenty Years After Prakash Singh — The Reform That Was Ordered and Never Delivered
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: The Supreme Court directed seven police reforms in 2006. Two decades on, forces run at roughly a fifth understrength and 86% of the state police is constabulary with one promotion in a career.

item.title: The Country That Stopped Counting Itself
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: India's last census was in 2011. Every welfare list, every seat allocation and every per-capita figure in public use rests on a population that no longer exists.

item.title: The Participation That Is Not Yet Employment
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: India’s female labour force participation rose eighteen percentage points in six years — the fastest improvement of any major economy. Almost none of it arrived as a wage.

item.title: The Capex Budget and the Capacity to Spend It
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: ₹12.22 lakh crore of capital expenditure against a 4.3% deficit. The Union Budget 2026-27 makes a coherent bet — and hands the binding constraint to the states.

item.title: The Largest Thing India Does Well
item.dc:creator: Pritiraj Brahma
item.description: India moves 64 crore people through a voting booth in six weeks without serious incident — the most impressive administrative act on earth. Everything surrounding that act is weaker than the act itself.
